evidence: The premise holds but the conclusion does not. Yes, every TaskRun output save carrying pr_url queues one process_inbox_pr_review job (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:126-139 -> products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:149-155), and ReviewRun has no (pull_request, head_sha) unique key (products/stamphog/backend/models.py:140-160; only delivery_id is unique at :145). But the consumer is serialized on the PullRequest row, not on the ReviewRun select_for_update the finding fixates on. Inside transaction.atomic(using=run_write_db) (tasks.py:1185) the first statement is _upsert_pull_request (tasks.py:1186), which runs BEFORE the head-keyed dedupe query (tasks.py:1202-1210) and the create (tasks.py:1223). _upsert_pull_request (tasks.py:319-363) either INSERTs the PR row via get_or_create (tasks.py:339-343; the uncommitted row plus the unique_stamphog_pull_request index at models.py:119-123 block a concurrent INSERT until commit, after which get_or_create re-selects and falls into the update branch) or runs the conditional UPDATE at tasks.py:349-353, whose row lock is held to commit (the docstring at tasks.py:322-325 and the webhook path's comment at tasks.py:1037-1044 both state this is the serialization point). Two concurrent inbox jobs for the same head therefore cannot both reach tasks.py:1202 before one commits; the loser's dedupe query then runs on a fresh READ COMMITTED snapshot, finds the winner's run at that head, and returns at tasks.py:1211-1221 (restarting only a stranded QUEUED run). The only lock-free exits from _upsert_pull_request are (a) incoming_updated_at is None (tasks.py:346-348), impossible here because get_pr returns GitHub's raw PR JSON unchanged (logic/github_client.py:466-474, _json at :458-462) and GET /pulls/{n} always carries updated_at; and (b) the UPDATE losing to a strictly newer stored clock (tasks.py:359-362), after which the recheck at tasks.py:1191-1197 bails before any create. Both models route to the same writer alias (posthog/product_db_router.py:37-41 is per app-label route, and get_or_create/update set _for_write), so the PR lock sits inside the same transaction as the run create. No production path bypasses this: the facade's create_review_run (facade/api.py:165-182) has zero non-test callers, and the only other ReviewRun.create is the webhook path (tasks.py:1056), which takes the same PR row lock via _upsert_pull_request at tasks.py:1035-1036; an opened delivery for a self-driving draft is pre-filtered at tasks.py:226-231 with the carve-out limited to head-changing actions (tasks.py:167-168), so the webhook never mints a second run at the initial head. Existing coverage: tests/test_tasks.py:992-1020 (refire dedupe at the current head, incl. QUEUED restart and FAILED recreate) and :483-516 (the locked-recheck seam). The requested concurrent-dispatch test is a hardening ask, not evidence of a bug. Consistent with cluster 42 (1/6 real).
notes: Would flip to real if a path reached ReviewRun.create at tasks.py:1223 without _upsert_pull_request having taken the PullRequest row (e.g. GitHub omitting updated_at from the PR object, or the tasks.py:1191-1197 recheck being removed), if a production caller of create_review_run or a direct ReviewRun.create outside that transaction appeared, or if PullRequest and ReviewRun were split across DB aliases so the lock fell outside the run-creating transaction.
